rationale_evidence.anchor: The analysis correctly rejects measure theory as the foundation, but it does not offer a **positive mathematical characterization** of the semantic/epistemic core.
rationale_evidence.statement: Endorses the category-error correction (measure theory is a tool, not the ontology of knowledge) as 'the single most important correction in the entire research program', and endorses the layered core->regime architecture, but identifies the gap that the semantic/epistemic core is left as a philosophical (not mathematical) definition; recommends characterizing it via relational structures (Roberts), logical structures (Fagin/Gärdenfors/Gelfond&Kahl), and institutional structures (Searle/Brandom) — mathematical structures (sets, relations, logics) but not measure-theoretic ones.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Concentrate on KnowledgeOS definition and empirical validation, not measure theory.
rationale_evidence.statement: Measure theory is declared 'properly scoped' (an external regime operating on projections, not the ontology, not a universal requirement, governed by Roberts' measurement criteria) and further foundational measure-theory work is judged premature without a stable core definition, empirical test cases, and concrete regime implementations. The KnowledgeOS core is assessed as conceptual but not formal across seven concepts (domain objects, participants, contexts, information, epistemic states, knowledge attributions, transitions), the regime model as conceptual but not concrete, Roberts' governance as identified but not applied, and empirical validation as non-existent.

rationale_evidence.anchor: An epistemic operator is not necessarily a primitive object. It is a **transition-generating capability** over epistemic states. ... The experiments were effectively asking: Which state-transition capabilities cannot be reconstructed from the others? That is a more rigorous question than: Which operator names are irreducible?
rationale_evidence.statement: Reinterprets epistemic operators (Hypothesize, Challenge, Revise, Qualify, Infer, each given a signature Op(E,...)->E') as transition-generating capabilities over epistemic states rather than primitive objects in themselves, reframing the kernel-reduction question from 'which operator names are irreducible' to 'which state-transition capabilities cannot be reconstructed from the others' -- judged a more rigorous question.

rationale_evidence.anchor: We should not optimize: |operator names|. Instead optimize: **minimal structure preserving required semantic behavior** ... define: $$\mathfrak R=\{\text{admissible representations of the epistemic structure}\}.$$ Two representations R_1,R_2 are equivalent if: R_1=_sem R_2 when they preserve the same required semantic behavior. This is exactly the missing level between representation and kernel.
rationale_evidence.statement: Explains the 13-vs-8 kernel-minimality instability as a category error (optimizing the count of operator NAMES rather than minimal structure preserving required semantic behaviour), proposing a space of admissible representations R and a semantic-equivalence relation R1 =_sem R2 as the missing level between raw representation and kernel minimality.

rationale_evidence.anchor: The probabilistic regime may construct (Omega,F,P) and derive: P(p|F_t)=0.93. But the core does **not** change: Knows(a,p,c,t) into: P(p|F_t)=0.93. Therefore: $$PosteriorAssessment\neq KnowledgeAttribution$$ This is one of the strongest architectural invariants we now have.
rationale_evidence.statement: Worked example connecting the regime architecture to the earlier measure-theoretic apparatus: a probabilistic regime may compute P(p|F_t)=0.93 as a projection over the core, but this NEVER changes the core relation Knows(a,p,c,t) into that number -- giving PosteriorAssessment != KnowledgeAttribution as one of the strongest architectural invariants reached so far.

## Rationale
Endorses the category-error correction (measure theory is a tool, not the ontology of knowledge) as 'the single most important correction in the entire research program', and endorses the layered core->regime architecture, but identifies the gap that the semantic/epistemic core is left as a philosophical (not mathematical) definition; recommends characterizing it via relational structures (Roberts), logical structures (Fagin/Gärdenfors/Gelfond&Kahl), and institutional structures (Searle/Brandom) — mathematical structures (sets, relations, logics) but not measure-theoretic ones [S0585]. Measure theory is declared 'properly scoped' (an external regime operating on projections, not the ontology, not a universal requirement, governed by Roberts' measurement criteria) and further foundational measure-theory work is judged premature without a stable core definition, empirical test cases, and concrete regime implementations. The KnowledgeOS core is assessed as conceptual but not formal across seven concepts (domain objects, participants, contexts, information, epistemic states, knowledge attributions, transitions), the regime model as conceptual but not concrete, Roberts' governance as identified but not applied, and empirical validation as non-existent [S0613]. Reinterprets epistemic operators (Hypothesize, Challenge, Revise, Qualify, Infer, each given a signature Op(E,...)->E') as transition-generating capabilities over epistemic states rather than primitive objects in themselves, reframing the kernel-reduction question from 'which operator names are irreducible' to 'which state-transition capabilities cannot be reconstructed from the others' -- judged a more rigorous question [S2371]. Explains the 13-vs-8 kernel-minimality instability as a category error (optimizing the count of operator NAMES rather than minimal structure preserving required semantic behaviour), proposing a space of admissible representations R and a semantic-equivalence relation R1 =_sem R2 as the missing level between raw representation and kernel minimality [S2371]. Worked example connecting the regime architecture to the earlier measure-theoretic apparatus: a probabilistic regime may compute P(p|F_t)=0.93 as a projection over the core, but this NEVER changes the core relation Knows(a,p,c,t) into that number -- giving PosteriorAssessment != KnowledgeAttribution as one of the strongest architectural invariants reached so far [S2371].
